traits.flowering_months.note: iNaturalist research-grade records on GBIF in the south and central Puget Sound lowlands (46.7 to 48.0° N, 122.0 to 123.1° W; counted 2026-10-14): 63 records annotated as flowering (May 7, Jun 35, Jul 15, Aug 4, Sep 2); stated as the months holding at least a tenth of them, May to July. FEIS (Symphoricarpos albus) gives May to August across the range, most in June and July. Idžojtić, Dendrology (2019) p. 655: flowers June to October. Not combined: Dendrology's months are for the tree grown in Europe, the spec's for its own range.

traits.fruiting_months.note: USA National Phenology Network observations (Nature's Notebook) at lowland sites west of the Cascades in Washington and Oregon (below 300 m, west of 121.8° W; 2009 to 2026, fetched 2026-10-14): 156 plant-years at 34 sites seen with ripe fruit, by the months they were seen in (Jan 46, Feb 33, Mar 22, Apr 5, May 1, Jul 23, Aug 52, Sep 64, Oct 78, Nov 84, Dec 61); stated as the months with at least a third as many as the busiest, August to February. FEIS (Symphoricarpos albus): ripe in late August and early September, and the berries often stay on over winter (the Seed Manual: until the next spring, unless eaten); so ripe berries are on the plant from August to February.

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960), as Symphoricarpos albus: grows 50 cm to 2.5 m tall.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960), as Symphoricarpos albus: leaves 1.5 cm to 3 cm long.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Symphoricarpos albus (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.63 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 1 record in 1 source); trunks 0.64, branches 0.61. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a low, twiggy shrub of thin stems with small, opposite, oval leaves and clusters of round white berries that last into winter. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 1.2 m tall at 12 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: dull blue-green leaves; white berries. Fruit (plant roadmap P4), as in mid-July: small clusters of berries at the twig tips, pale green turning white. Its year (appearance.organs.bloom.season) takes its days of bud, flower, fruit, ripe and fall from the months it flowers and fruits in, by the rules at the flowering plants (development, 2026-10-14); until then they were authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands: small pink bells in May to July; berries green, white from August, hanging through the winter. The forest's packages show day 196 (mid-July) until the phenology of plant roadmap P5 sets the day from the date and the local climate.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

appearance.organs.bloom.season.flower_lo.note: Its flowers drawn one by one (spec rework L1b): small pink to white bell-shaped flowers 4 to 7 mm long, drawn as closed bells. From general descriptions of the species (OregonFlora, the Flora of North America and nursery and extension pages as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read). The size is the flower's width, or a closed corolla's length, over the fruit's length, roughly as in life.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 437, Symphoricarpos albus: leaf arrangement opposite.
